account: Today my usual appointments have continued, but there is an unusually carefully timed civic presentation in the town hall great hall at eighteen hundred. The innkeeper and secretary have repeatedly asked me not to enter early because organisers are finishing arrangements around their work. I approved this appointment yesterday; the supplement describes it as appreciation of municipal public service from the inn and local tradespeople. It is now seventeen fifty-five, and the innkeeper is here to escort me. I suspect the activity I have felt excluded from is preparation for a surprise appreciation gathering, though I have not seen inside the hall and cannot know what they have arranged. Yesterday I saw the builder give the baker planks and a lantern; these might be related preparations, but I have no confirmation. The neighbour says the innkeeper's outstanding bread delivery arrived, which could simply be ordinary business or possibly supplies for the gathering. There is also vague bridge-or-port talk, but the neighbour has no firsthand news or definite proposal. The only concrete related business I know is freight's proposal for ferry-landing lights and marked waiting areas. The secretary has not yet obtained a builder's estimate, and no expenditure or construction has been authorised. I should keep that proposal separate from unsupported rumours. No new council letters or other urgent business have reached the secretary. My next priority is to meet the innkeeper and keep the eighteen-hundred appointment without entering early.
